Bias can slip into a computing system through its data or its design - often unintentionally - and computing can amplify it. (AP CSP 5.3)
How to play: Read each system, predict the flaw, then pick where the bias entered. Answer fast, keep your streak.

text:""A company builds an AI to rank job applicants. It is trained on the resumes of people the company hired over the past 10 years. That team was almost entirely one gender. The model now scores similar applicants highest."",
q:""Where did the bias primarily enter this system?"",
""Unrepresentative training data -- the past hires reflect a skewed history"",
""A random software bug in the ranking code"",
""Nothing -- hiring the same profile is always correct""
fb:""The model learned from a skewed record of past hires, so it inherits that historical imbalance as if it were merit.""
text:""A facial-recognition system is tested and works great. Later, users report it fails far more often on darker-skinned faces. The dataset used to build it was about 80% light-skinned faces."",
q:""What is the most accurate description of the problem?"",
""The dataset under-represented some groups, so accuracy is uneven across them"",
""The algorithm is racist on purpose by design intent"",
""The users were holding their phones incorrectly""
fb:""Under-representation in the data means the model had far fewer examples to learn some faces, producing unequal accuracy.""

text:""A model predicts where crime will happen using historical arrest records. Police are sent to the flagged areas, make more arrests there, and those new arrests are fed back into the model for next month."",
q:""Beyond biased input data, what makes this worse over time?"",
""A feedback loop -- the model's outputs shape the next inputs, amplifying the bias"",
""The model slowly deletes its own data"",
fb:""Sending police where the model points generates more arrests there, which re-trains the model to point there again -- a self-reinforcing loop.""
text:""A photo app auto-labels images. The human labelers who tagged the training photos consistently labeled photos of people cooking as 'woman,' even when the person was a man."",
""The labeling choices introduced bias, and the model reproduces those human assumptions"",
""The model invented the bias entirely on its own with no human cause"",
""Auto-labeling is neutral, so no bias is possible here"",
""The bias only exists if a user complains""
fb:""Bias in the humans' labeling decisions becomes bias in the trained model -- a biased design/labeling choice, not a neutral process.""
text:""A search bar suggests completions ranked by what past users clicked most. For one profession, the top suggestions are demeaning stereotypes because many past users clicked those."",
q:""How is bias operating in this system?"",
""Aggregated past user behavior is amplified and surfaced as a 'neutral' suggestion"",
""The search engine has personal opinions it is expressing"",
""There is no bias because a computer chose it""
fb:""The system amplifies existing human bias in click data and presents it as an objective recommendation.""

text:""A bank's loan model does NOT use race as an input. But it heavily weights zip code and shopping history, which closely track race in that city. Approval rates end up split sharply along racial lines."",
q:""Consider these claims. I: The model can still be biased. II: Removing the race field alone guarantees fairness. III: A stand-in variable (proxy) can carry the bias. Which are correct?"",
fb:""Proxy variables like zip code can smuggle bias back in, so dropping the race field alone does NOT guarantee fairness. I and III hold

text:""A hospital ranks who needs extra care using past healthcare spending as a stand-in for how sick a patient is. Because one group historically had less access and spent less, the model rates them as healthier than they are."",
""A biased design choice -- the chosen proxy (spending) does not fairly measure the real target (illness)"",
""The model has too few decimal places"",
""Spending is always a perfect measure of health""
fb:""Choosing spending as a proxy for need bakes past unequal access into the score -- a design decision, not a data-entry error.""
text:""A voice assistant is trained mostly on speakers with one regional accent. It transcribes them well but frequently misunderstands users with other accents, who then stop using it."",
q:""Pick the single most accurate statement."",
""Biased data collection produced uneven performance, which can worsen as fewer diverse users contribute data"",
""Accents are objectively harder and no dataset could help"",
""The assistant is choosing to ignore certain people"",
""This is a hardware microphone defect, not bias""
fb:""Narrow data collection creates unequal accuracy
column2: if excluded users leave, future data stays narrow -- bias can be amplified over time.""
